## Overview

Offline embedding refresh jobs are scheduled batch processes that regenerate vector embeddings for a corpus when the underlying embedding model changes or source documents update in bulk. Rather than re-embedding on-demand, they operate on a fixed cadence and re-embed the full or incremental document set, then atomically swap the new vectors into the retrieval index to avoid serving mixed-model results mid-transition.

## Key Characteristics

- **Scheduled execution**: Run on fixed cadence rather than on-demand
- **Batch scope**: Re-embed the full or incremental document set in a single job
- **Atomic swaps**: Exchange vectors into the retrieval index atomically to prevent mixed-model results during transition
- **Bulk triggers**: Regenerate when the underlying embedding model changes or when source documents update in bulk

## Operational Concerns

### Model Versioning
Version the embedding model per batch so that each refresh job can be traced to the model version that produced it. This enables auditing, rollback analysis, and debugging of model-related quality issues.

### Vector Drift Monitoring
Monitor drift between old and new vectors to detect quality regressions or unexpected model behaviour. Tracking magnitude and distribution of changes helps identify whether a new model has fundamentally altered the embedding space.

### Blue/Green Index Staging
Stage the swap behind a blue/green index strategy so that a quality regression can be rolled back without downtime. This allows validation of the new embedding set before it becomes the live index, and provides a quick fallback if issues are detected post-swap.
